name: Moon-dust airlock trap
subtitle: charged curtains that strip dust off spacesuits

effects.effect: a material holds a permanent electric charge that grabs dust

effect: a material holds a permanent electric charge that grabs dust
how: Moon dust is sharp, clingy and electrically charged; on Apollo it ground into suit joints and got into the astronauts' lungs, and months-long stays will be far worse. Before entering the habitat an astronaut stands while puffs of air shake dust off the suit, and curtains of permanently charged fibres, like mask filter material, grab the already-charged grains before they reach the cabin.
obstacle: The curtains clog fast, so they must be cheap to swap or clean without bringing the dust inside.
why: Charged dust meets charged fibre with no power needed; it targets a top lunar-base problem.
real: Patents describe airlock dust-removal systems that neutralize suit dust and trap it in a filter under the astronaut's platform, and NASA tested airlock filtration, but no electret-curtain capture was found.
